status: Written and hashed before any Indus numeral was read or any comparison was run. Not yet runnable: the Indus numeral source is not confirmed.
question: Does the Indus stroke-numeral system share a base structure (decimal, vigesimal, quinary, or other) with one language family more than with others?

languages.Dravidian: numeralbank/numerals cldf, Dravidian (62 languages), CC BY 4.0
languages.Austroasiatic: numeralbank/numerals cldf, Austroasiatic (165 languages), CC BY 4.0
languages.Semitic: numeralbank/numerals cldf, Afro-Asiatic subset: Hebrew, Aramaic dialects, Arabic varieties, Amharic, Maltese (CC BY 4.0)

indus_side: Stroke numerals only, read from a licensed source to be confirmed (Mayig corpus, MIT/Apache, unverified for stroke numerals). ICIT is metadata-only and excluded.
statistic: Base type for each language, coded from its number words for 1-10 and 10, 20, 100, using a fixed rule written before the coding. For Indus: base implied by the stroke sequence and any composite sign for 10.
null: Shuffled base labels across languages within each family (1,000 draws). A family match counts only if its observed match rate is above the 95th percentile of the shuffled rate.
falsifier: Indus base agrees with no family above the null, or the Indus side cannot be coded from the source (stroke numerals only up to 7 may not determine a base). Either result is reported as inconclusive or negative.
controls: Coverage imbalance: Austroasiatic and Afro-Asiatic have more languages than Indo-Aryan. Use equal-sized random subsamples of 10 languages per family. Report the family sizes.
